title: An event bus with variance
description:
Write a message bus where a handler for a base type also receives messages of derived types, thanks to contravariance:

- `public interface IHandler<in T> { void Handle(T message); }`
- `public class Bus` with `Subscribe(object handler)` (any object implementing one or more `IHandler<...>`), `Unsubscribe(object handler)` and `int Publish<T>(T message)` that calls `Handle` on every subscribed handler that is an `IHandler<T>`, in subscription order, and returns how many handled it.
- A handler that throws does not stop the others; `Publish` collects the exceptions and, after calling everyone, throws an `AggregateException` with them.

The message records and some handlers are defined for you.
hints: With `in T` on the interface, a `Log` (an `IHandler<Event>`) also *is* an `IHandler<Click>`, so `h is IHandler<T> handler` finds it for a `Click` (lesson 8.05).
Loop over a copy (`_handlers.ToList()`), wrap each `Handle` call in `try`/`catch`, and throw one `AggregateException` at the end if anything failed.
